headline: City commuters express confusion as new 'Protest Permit' booths require a notarized loyalty oath to the weather
body:
"I just wanted to hold a sign about the rising cost of onions, but the officer at the desk told me I first had to sign a 400-page affidavit confirming that I have no personal grievances against the monsoon clouds," said a local IT consultant waiting in line at the Jantar Mantar kiosk.

"The form asked if I was protesting on behalf of myself or if I was merely a temporary atmospheric disturbance, and honestly, after standing in this heat for three hours, I feel like both," remarked a college student clutching his laminated permission slip.

"Business has been slow, but at least the police now require all protesters to buy a cold bottle of water from my stall as part of their mandatory 'civic hydration' compliance protocol," noted a nearby street vendor.

"I tried to chant a slogan, but the permit clearly states I can only recite the official 'Sunlight Appreciation' lyrics provided by the municipal authorities, so I spent the afternoon humming in alphabetical order," shared a retired government clerk.

"It’s quite efficient, really; now that everyone has a permit, the police just check our expiration dates before deciding whether to provide us with a police van ride home or an Uber voucher," added a daily wage laborer.
caption: From mandatory weather oaths to hydration compliance, the new protest permit process is definitely... something. #Delhi #ProtestCulture #Bureaucracy (satire)
igHook: Would you sign a 400-page oath just to hold a protest sign?
imagePrompt: A nondescript metal booth with a long queue of people holding clipboards standing on a dusty urban sidewalk next to a barricade.

sourceHeadline.title: Concerned by reports of mass detentions, UN says about Delhi police's crackdown on CJP protest
